article_title: Examining the Relations Between Self-Regulation and Achievement in Third-Grade Students
citation: Day, Stephanie L.; Connor, Carol M. (2017). Examining the relations between self-regulation and achievement in third grade students. Assessment for Effective Intervention, 42(2), 97-109. https://doi.org/10.1177/1534508416670367
title: Remembering Rules and Regulation Picture Task (RRRP)
description: The RRRP is a direct, individually administered self-regulation assessment in which children place colored blocks on objects in a park picture in a specified order, waiting for 'go' and, in the second half, switching blue for red blocks. The authors report that "The RRRP can be administered in approximately 7 minutes," that inter-rater reliability was .95 (Kappa), and that overall scale reliability was .97. It was designed for use beyond first grade, where the HTKS reaches ceiling.
requirements: A trained tester reads directions aloud and administers the 10 items one-on-one, taking about 7 minutes per child
constraints: The authors note there was some evidence the RRRP may be too easy for some children, and that it must be administered to a larger and more diverse sample and in other grades
target_learners: third grade students (designed to extend to children beyond first grade)
target_learning_goals: assessment of self-regulation skills (working memory, attentional flexibility, inhibitory control)
examples: In the study, the RRRP was administered to 282 third graders from 34 classrooms in fall and spring, with examiners recording correctness, waiting for 'go', and repetitions
key_sources: Day, Stephanie L.; Connor, Carol M. (2017). Examining the relations between self-regulation and achievement in third grade students. Assessment for Effective Intervention, 42(2), 97-109. https://doi.org/10.1177/1534508416670367

article_title: Spelling development in young children: A case of representational redescription?
citation: Critten, S., Pine, K., & Steffler, D. (2006). Spelling Development in Young Children: A Case of Representational-Redescription? Manuscript submitted for publication (Date of Submission: Thursday 3rd August 2006).
title: Karmiloff-Smith's Representational-Redescription model applied to spelling development
description: The RR model describes how knowledge is represented and changes with development through four levels: Implicit (behavioral mastery without understanding or verbal access), E1 (abstraction of an internal theory that dominates external data, producing overgeneralization errors and U-shaped performance), E2 (integration of theory with environmental data with improved performance), and E3 (fully explicit, verbalizable, flexible knowledge). Applied to spelling, E1 children over-apply phonological (E1A) or morphological -ed (E1B) theories, and E3 children can "recognize exceptions to those rules" such as -ed being only for regular verbs.
requirements: Children's verbal justifications about spelling choices must be elicited and coded, since levels beyond Implicit are indexed by explanation quality, not accuracy alone
constraints: Development through RR levels is domain specific to spelling (and possibly reading), not indicative of similar development in domains such as numeracy
No children in this study were predominantly at the Implicit level, so U-shaped performance at the representational level could not be commented upon
target_learners: young children aged 5-7 learning to spell
target_learning_goals: phonological and morphological spelling knowledge, including the -ed past-tense convention and its exceptions
examples: Children at E1B justified choices with the -ed rule, e.g. explaining that slepted was correct "it has an -ed", while an E3 child explained called was correct because "it has the word call with an -ed on the end to make it past (tense)"
key_sources: Critten, S., Pine, K., & Steffler, D. (2006). Spelling Development in Young Children: A Case of Representational-Redescription? Manuscript submitted for publication (Date of Submission: Thursday 3rd August 2006). https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.99.1.207
